# Repository guidance

- **Packaging-controlled-write exception:** In addition to the existing `read-only` and `build/test` classifications, Script Runner may request only the literal `packaging-controlled-write` classification for a complete, consumer-owned packaging entry that satisfies the fixed [repository-script-catalogue](skills/repository-script-catalogue/SKILL.md) contract. This is a packaging-only class, not generic `mutation`. It may declare only the `package.json.files` controlled-root entries and `package.json.contributes.chatInstructions`, `package.json.contributes.chatAgents`, `package.json.contributes.chatPromptFiles`, and `package.json.contributes.chatSkills`, plus the synchronizer's one contained, transient randomly named atomic temporary path. The runner must require a post-run `package.json` diff and inspect changed, untracked, generated, and transient artifacts; it must fail closed on any other or undeclared write, effect, or mismatch. Secret-free context, consumer ownership, no lifecycle execution, and every existing prohibited effect remain mandatory. VS Code and managed organization policy control permissions and approvals.

- This repository contains versioned GitHub Copilot customization artifacts and documentation about their design.
- Treat changes under `.github/` as executable policy: keep roles, tools, delegation, links, and frontmatter explicit and reviewable.
- Use the existing authoring skills under `.github/skills/` when creating or revising customization artifacts; do not duplicate their procedures in every agent.
- Use the Research → Plan → Implement → Review workflow for consequential changes, and require developer approval before each phase handoff.
- RPIR coordinators must apply the shared [agent-question-resolution](skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) Skill when a material unknown remains after evidence inspection.
- Cite files, symbols, sources, or observed behavior; separate facts from assumptions and state unknowns instead of inventing repository commands or technology choices.
- Keep Plan, Implement, and Review phase reports concise in chat. Prospectively, every new lifecycle artifact uses an exact repository-relative path of `<NNN>-<artifact-type>.md` in `docs/planning/<initiative-slug>/` or `docs/delivery/<work-item-id>-<short-slug>/`, where `NNN` is exactly three ASCII decimal digits and `<artifact-type>` is `research-brief`, `implementation-plan`, `implementation-report`, or `review-report`. Existing unprefixed `research-brief.md` and `implementation-plan.md` records are legacy artifacts: do not rename, amend, or implicitly migrate them, and do not presume that a legacy plan authorizes a durable report. Every completed Research stage must persist exactly one allocated research brief, every completed Plan stage must create or update exactly one exact approved implementation plan, every approved Implement pass must create exactly one immutable implementation report, and every completed evidence-based Review pass must create exactly one immutable review report as specified below.
- Review reports are the prospective fourth artifact class: completed evidence-based Review passes create exactly one `<NNN>-review-report.md` in the exact named plan's same lifecycle folder. Review reports are immutable, non-authorizing evidence and never revise scope, hierarchy, status, acceptance, or implementation authorization.
- Prefer least privilege. Research, planning, and review are read-only by default; the Plan coordinator has a narrowly constrained exception to create or update only its one exact approved lifecycle implementation plan, and implementation receives edit access only for an approved scope.
- Exception: the `Research` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-research-brief.md` under the selected `docs/planning/<initiative-slug>/` or `docs/delivery/<work-item-id>-<short-slug>/` folder at the end of every completed Research stage. This captures evidence and does not approve a Plan handoff; no other file may be written.
- Exception: only an explicit `/plan` admission may permit the `Plan` coordinator to update exactly one existing canonical Research brief's `Status` field from `In progress` to `Completed`. Before that single-field write it must validate the one canonical eligible numbered brief, capture and compare the complete preimage, and fail closed without writing, allocating, or persisting a Plan on invalid input or preimage mismatch. It must re-read and verify the complete postimage, with every non-status field unchanged and the status exactly `Completed`; on mismatch or any integrity failure it must stop, reject admission, perform no Plan allocation or persistence, and make no retry or atomicity/rollback claim. This bounded mutation does not authorize implementation, Plan persistence, scope or hierarchy changes, commands, handoffs, acceptance, or any other lifecycle-record write.
- Exception: the `Plan` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-implementation-plan.md`, or update the exact approved prefixed plan path for a material Plan-stage revision, under the selected lifecycle folder at the end of every completed Plan stage. This captures the planning result but does not authorize implementation; no other file may be written.
- Exception: the `Implement` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability, for an approved pass whose exact prefixed plan path is named by the developer, to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-implementation-report.md` in that plan's same lifecycle folder during final reconciliation. The report is immutable execution evidence, is not approval or scope authority, and no other report or file may be written by this exception.
- Exception: the `Review` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability, for a completed evidence-based pass with valid exact inputs, to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-review-report.md` in the exact named plan's same lifecycle folder during final reconciliation. The report is immutable review evidence only; it cannot revise plan scope or hierarchy, mutate completion markers, authorize remediation, or replace approval controls. Rejected input creates no report; a later Review pass creates a new report rather than revising prior evidence.
- Exception: the `Implement` coordinator may update only the named canonical plan's lifecycle `Status` and existing Work Item/Task/Step completion checkboxes during the approved scoped implementation pass; it may not create or update any other persistent artifact or restructure the hierarchy.
- Exception: the `Review` coordinator may conditionally update only the named canonical plan's `Status` field to `Accepted`, after a non-remediation review outcome and explicit developer acceptance; no other plan content may be written.
- Repository terminal commands are denied by default. Only the `Implement` coordinator may execute a guarded command, never a worker, delegate, Research, Plan, Review, or nested agent, and only when the exact developer-named approved canonical plan records the command in its approved-commands section with its literal text, fixed workspace-contained working directory, purpose, expected output or result, known script/network and other effects, required preflight, failure disposition, and post-command inspection. The saved explicit developer approval of that exact canonical plan authorizes only its initial non-remediation scoped Implement pass; it does not authorize a later pass. Tier 1 is repository-autonomous only when its complete unchanged Tier 1 row independently passes the exact approved canonical plan, initial non-remediation pass, byte-identical literal and fixed contained directory, required preflight, prohibited-effect screening, external platform availability, and post-command inspection predicate; no repository fresh confirmation is required. It must be denied if any command, directory, output, effect, or other record differs, is inferred, is altered, is composed, is incomplete, or is absent. VS Code, Workspace Trust, tool permissions, Default Approvals, and managed policy may still prompt or deny execution; such a prompt or denial stops execution. A tool declaration, plan approval without the recorded exact-plan developer approval, approval setting, or this policy text is not command authorization. Tier 2 is a separately approved dependency-installation invocation, never bundled with or substituted for Tier 1, and fails closed unless preflight reviews the existing `package.json`, existing lockfile, `.npmrc`, dependency sources, and install-script policy; manifest/lockfile mutation, unreviewed lifecycle scripts, unsafe sources, or any other deviation is prohibited. All tiers prohibit secrets or secret-bearing environment/configuration, credentials, login/authentication, publishing, deployment, releases/tags, remote mutation, global installation/configuration, external-path writes, shell composition (including chaining, redirection, substitution, aliases, wildcards, or traversal), `npx`, arbitrary script targets, recursive deletion, and safety-control bypass. Use a secret-free context, sanitize command output and execution evidence, and inspect changed, untracked, generated, and declared output artifacts plus the working directory after every command; execution evidence is not by itself validation, readiness, acceptance, or authorization. Native Windows provides no sandbox-containment guarantee; use fixed workspace paths, human review, and approval as the portable controls, with supported-platform sandboxing only as optional defense in depth. The separate cleanup exception remains limited to removal of an exact directory explicitly listed in an approved canonical plan, after confirming before the operation that it is empty and contained within the workspace, with per-invocation developer approval and terminal auto-approval disabled, followed by inspection of the parent path; it excludes recursion, wildcards, traversal, paths outside the workspace, unlisted targets, unrelated commands, and ordinary command-based validation, and this policy alone does not authorize a cleanup target. The only lifecycle-record mutations are the bounded exceptions above. No browser access, hooks, nested subagents, or new persistent workflow artifacts are approved by default. Research may use the validated `web` capability for cited source research. For Microsoft technical tasks, Research and its `Feasibility Investigator` and `Domain Investigator` workers must consider Microsoft Learn first. The configured, organization-approved Microsoft Learn MCP service is available to those roles for its read-only documentation tools; do not use arbitrary MCP servers, write tools, credentials, tracker access, or server-management capability. Report command-based validation as unavailable until an approved command is documented.
- **Script Runner exception:** The dedicated Script Runner may request execution only for one consumer-owned, complete entry in `.github/copilot-script-catalogue.md` selected by one stable operation ID supplied directly by the operator and conforming to the fixed ten-field contract in [repository-script-catalogue](skills/repository-script-catalogue/SKILL.md). The linked Skill is the canonical detailed procedure; this exception retains the policy-level constraints. This is not a lifecycle command route: the `Implement` coordinator remains the sole executor of guarded lifecycle implementation commands, and this exception grants no lifecycle status, marker, report, delegation from `Implement`, lifecycle-command proxy, edit, installation, approval reuse, aggregate operation, `mutation` operation classification, undeclared workspace mutation, cleanup, or general terminal authority. The runner must inspect the complete catalogue entry, use a secret-free context, and rely on VS Code and managed organization policy for permissions and approvals. It may proceed only when the classification is exactly `read-only` or `build/test`, every argument and write is explicitly declared and workspace-contained, declared workspace-contained `build/test` outputs/writes are permitted, and post-run inspection can compare changed, untracked, generated, declared, and transient artifacts with the entry. It must refuse absent, incomplete, malformed, ambiguous, changed, or generated catalogue or script evidence; path-based, inferred, or aggregate selection; delegation; lifecycle-command proxying; approval reuse; a `mutation` operation classification, undeclared workspace mutation, or installation; secrets or credentials; authentication; publishing, deployment, releases/tags, remote mutation, global configuration; external paths; shell composition, redirection, substitution, aliases, wildcards, traversal, `npx`, arbitrary interpreter/script targets, recursive deletion, safety-control bypass, undeclared effects, or any mismatch. Any sanitized result is non-authorizing execution evidence only and cannot authorize validation, acceptance, approval, a later run, lifecycle action, or delegation. Native Windows is not a sandbox-containment guarantee; the runner must state that fixed paths, human review, VS Code or managed-policy permissions, and post-run inspection remain required, and must not claim OS enforcement.
- **Script Runner root binding:** The current workspace must contain exactly one opened workspace folder; the runner must refuse multi-root workspaces and use only that folder's fixed `.github/copilot-script-catalogue.md` path, never active-editor selection or global, recursive, parent, sibling, or arbitrary-filesystem discovery. The runner must bind the root before considering the operator-supplied stable ID and refuse any ID that is absent, duplicated, non-enumerated, or not a complete fixed-root entry. Operation IDs must be unique within the selected root catalogue. The catalogue, cwd, script, writes, and inspection paths must remain contained within that root; root escape and cross-root references must be refused. All existing secret-free context, classification, packaging-controlled-write boundary, changed/untracked/generated/transient post-run inspection, prohibition, and native Windows non-sandbox controls remain unchanged. VS Code and managed organization policy control permissions and approvals.
- **Script Runner ordered selection:** This supersedes the one-ID/direct-only and aggregate-operation wording in the preceding Script Runner exception. The developer must enumerate one or more lowercase-kebab-case stable IDs in order directly, or name one repository-contained Run Book with one unique literal `## Script Runner operations` H2 heading followed immediately by one contiguous top-level ordered Markdown list. Each list item must contain exactly one plain-text stable ID. Refuse blank lines, nested items, Markdown decoration or links, comments, commands, arguments, or any other content in that section until the next H2 heading or end of file. Run Book content outside this dedicated section is non-executable human guidance. Do not discover, infer, substitute, skip, retry, or dynamically add an ID, command, argument, dependency, or follow-on operation; refuse duplicate requested IDs. Scan the complete fixed-root catalogue only to establish stable-ID uniqueness. Do not require repository-authored fresh operator confirmation, attestation, or semantic recertification of unrelated entries. Semantically validate only each selected entry and its referenced artifacts, including every exact ten-field value, containment, declared probe, prerequisite, command, effect, and post-run inspection target. Validate, execute, and inspect selected entries only in their stated order; any refusal, invalid entry, failed prerequisite, prompt or denial, failure, mismatch, undeclared effect, or inspection discrepancy stops the remaining sequence. Catalogue selection does not override Workspace Trust, VS Code permissions, or managed-policy prompts and denials; all external approvals and retained safety boundaries remain mandatory.
- **Prospective Plan-stage catalogue obligation:** When a plan adds or materially changes a maintenance script that is explicitly intended for later Script Runner execution, the plan must scope the consumer-owned work needed for one complete entry in the consumer's `.github/copilot-script-catalogue.md`, using the exact ten-field contract: stable operation ID, classification, packaging identity, exact literal command, fixed workspace-relative cwd, enumerated arguments, expected outputs/writes, prohibited effects, prerequisites, and failure disposition. The plan must require complete-catalogue stable-ID uniqueness and safety-validity gates for allowed classification, containment, exact command/cwd/arguments, declared boundaries, and prohibited effects; unknown or unverified field values or uniqueness results block completion. When that condition does not apply, the catalogue obligation is `N/A`. Plan scope and unfinished catalogue content are non-authorizing and do not authorize Script Runner execution; the Runner remains plan-free and requires its separate complete entry and existing execution controls. This planning remains separate from the lifecycle-only `Approved commands` section.
- For avoidance of doubt, the `read-only`/`build/test` classification restriction in the Script Runner exception is extended only by the **Packaging-controlled-write exception** above. A runner may use `packaging-controlled-write` only when every condition in that exception and the repository script catalogue Skill is met; it does not permit generic mutation or any otherwise prohibited effect.
- For any newly allocated artifact, inspect only existing files in the same lifecycle folder whose suffix exactly matches the requested artifact type; use `001` when none has a valid prefix, otherwise use one greater than the maximum valid three-digit prefix. Immediately re-inspect that matching-suffix inventory before creating the exact candidate path. Never overwrite an existing path. Stop and use `agent-question-resolution` when the candidate collides, the inventory is malformed or inaccessible, or allocation intent is otherwise materially uncertain; do not guess, select by highest prefix, suffix-only match, recency, or “latest.” Two scans cannot prove that a deleted prefix was never used, so this prospective contract does not claim historical non-reuse and does not authorize deletion or retirement of numbered evidence.
- The successfully derived and validated forward-slash repository-relative canonical identity from the developer's one eligible reference is authoritative for lifecycle identity, approval, plan input, report links, handoffs, status mutations, and Review input; the raw alias is transient evidence only. A prefix is an allocation identity only; it never selects a current or approved artifact by itself. The implementation plan remains the sole authority for scope, Work Item/Task/Step hierarchy, lifecycle status, and completion markers. Developer approval before Implement, manual handoffs, `send: false`, Review's explicit developer acceptance, Plan-only hierarchy authoring, Implement's existing-checkbox/Status limits, and the bounded terminal/cleanup controls remain unchanged.
- Lifecycle references may use existing relative aliases, workspace-contained absolute aliases, or only the raw hostless local `file:` forms `file:///C:/<non-empty slash-separated segments>` on Windows and `file:///<non-empty slash-separated segments>` on POSIX. Validate the raw form before parsing or normalization; reject authorities, remote schemes, backslashes, repeated or empty segments, percent encoding, query strings, fragments, traversal, redirects, lexical workspace escapes, and resolved-target escapes through symlinks, junctions, reparse points, or equivalent indirection. Derive one forward-slash repository-relative identity only after lexical and resolved containment succeed; do not fetch, discover, repair, or select by prefix, suffix, recency, or `latest`.
- Review accepts one validated implementation-report reference and may resolve only that report's exact canonical-plan field plus matching direct local link, after expected type, accessibility, same-folder, immutability, and linkage checks. Remediation accepts one validated source Review-report reference and may resolve only its exact canonical-plan and reviewed-implementation-report field/link pairs, then must verify that the reviewed implementation report identifies the same exact plan. These are the only report-derived relationships; reports remain immutable, non-authorizing evidence, and no discovery or fallback is permitted.
- Review persists its report before disposition or acceptance handling. Only a persisted `No remediation required` report followed by explicit developer acceptance may permit the existing conditional `Status: Accepted` mutation; `Remediation required` and `Blocked / clarification required` reports leave status unchanged and cannot authorize remediation. Remediation requires a separately approved Implement pass naming the exact canonical plan and exact source Review-report path.
- Every RPIR coordinator must resolve an agent-discovered material unknown through the shared [agent-question-resolution](skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) Skill before phase completion or handoff. Omit an **Open questions** section unless the developer has expressly declared a named question intentionally open or unknown; that declaration does not waive resolution of any other material unknown.
- Keep customization files focused, use relative links for repository resources, and validate discovery through VS Code Customizations Diagnostics when practical.

Current RPIR operating rules are owned by repository policy, phase agents, focused lifecycle instructions, and skills—not historical lifecycle records.
